comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences (Pedagogische wetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated normal full-time Dutch bachelor and its adopted regulations total 60+60+60=180 EC. Academic Skills A–D are compulsory zero-separate-credit components integrated into the credited courses. The degree includes a 6 EC internship, 15 EC empirical thesis and 30 EC open space; no particular minor, exchange or placement host is assumed. The separate UPvA teacher-education programme is not combined with this route.

components.name: Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 1
Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 2
components.note: Academic Skills A and B are compulsory in year 1. They carry no separate EC: their workload is credited within the content courses.

components.name: Bachelor Internship in Pedagogical Sciences
components.note: The normal programme requires a 6 EC internship, including approved practice or research experience, preparation, reflection and supervision. The course entry also offers a 9 EC variant; this example uses the prescribed 6 EC component. Students arrange an approved host and complete the required information and application training before starting.

components.name: Policy and Organisation of Childrearing and Education
Research in Practice
components.note: Year 2 requires at least 42 first-year EC. Academic Skills C and D are compulsory with no separate EC. Testing and Measurement follows participation in Descriptive Statistics; Inferential Statistics requires passing Descriptive Statistics; Research in Practice requires passing both Descriptive Statistics and Testing and Measurement. Professional Skills 2 requires passing Professional Skills 1.

components.name: Empirical Bachelor Thesis in Pedagogical Sciences
components.note: The 15 EC empirical thesis follows completion of the first two years, except that one year-2 content course and Academic Skills D may remain. At least nine colloquium points are also required for graduation: five from POW master-thesis presentations, one from a doctorate or inaugural lecture, and three from POW or Comenius lectures or conferences.

components.name: Professional Skills 3
components.note: Professional Skills 3 requires passing Professional Skills 2 and following Diagnostics. Following means a recorded assessment result. It develops practical child and adolescent assessment and advice skills.

components.name: Open Choice: Electives or Minor
components.note: The 30 EC open space remains unspecified. Choices must not overlap the compulsory curriculum. Second- and third-year faculty courses can be selected without extra approval. First-year courses normally need to form part of a completed minor; other choices, skills and language courses require prior Examination Board approval. Exchange also requires approval.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option balances developmental and social psychology with research, ethics, policy and community teaching. The exact-target interests also support coherent developmental-difficulty/support and family/social-context priorities. Their curricula have substantive differences and each pair passes the thirty-EC floor. Three is the maximum; no specialist clinical qualification is claimed.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine language and reading development and difficulties. UvA also addresses mathematics, school support and educational interventions; UCR focuses on language processing and experimental psycholinguistics.
Both connect nervous-system function and behaviour. UvA situates this study in the pedagogical curriculum; UCR provides a broad introductory brain-and-behaviour foundation.

Both study social relationships, group influences and behaviour as contexts of development. UvA specifically examines children’s peers and leisure, including developmental risks and protection; UCR studies social processes more broadly.
Both develop inferential statistical reasoning and analysis for behavioural or social research. UCR includes experimental design and multivariable modelling.
Both examine psychological difficulties, their explanations, risk and treatment. UvA focuses on developmental psychopathology in childhood and adolescence; UCR covers disorders across the lifespan.

Both develop diagnostic reasoning, selection and interpretation of tests and interviews, ethical awareness and case-based assessment. UvA focuses on child and pedagogical contexts; UCR combines broader introductory psychodiagnostics with psychotherapy.
Both study physical, cognitive, emotional and social development, its theories and environmental influences. UCR continues across adulthood, while UvA concentrates on conception through adolescence.

Both examine how educators and educational environments support children’s development. UCR creates teacher resources for resilience and inclusion; UvA compares educator roles, relationships and quality across childcare, school and youth care.
Both examine qualitative research questions and methods, interpretation and research quality. UCR develops broader qualitative social inquiry.
Both examine policy theories, processes, actors and analysis. UvA applies them to education and youth care; UCR uses a different policy case and policy-memo practice.
Both develop research design, measurement, sampling, validity and an empirical research cycle. UCR uses a broader student project rather than a specifically pedagogical focus.

Both critically examine ethical theories, values and competing interests. UvA applies philosophical argument specifically to education, childrearing, rights and paternalism; UCR supplies broader moral theory.

Both provide child-focused practical experience and reflection. UCR works with primary-school partners on rhetorical teaching and coaching; UvA requires an approved internship with broader pedagogical practice or research and formal supervision.

UCR Research Methods & Statistics contains descriptive statistics but is placed with Research Methodology as its strongest overall relationship. It is not counted a second time here.
Rhetoric and inclusive communication complement professional interaction but do not directly reproduce the structured basic counselling, listening and reflective interview training.

Selected assessment and research courses cover measurement, reliability and validity, but their strongest overall placements are Diagnostics and Research Methodology; no separate testing module is counted here.
Sociology and developmental psychology provide context, but no selected course centres family pedagogy, transactional parent-child interactions, parenting support and maltreatment.
Personality development is part of Lifespan Developmental Psychology, placed with Developmental Psychology. No separate selected course centres personality theory.
No selected course directly reproduces the advanced child and adolescent interviewing and creative professional conversation sequence.
General philosophy and research methods provide foundations, but no selected course centres philosophy of scientific explanation and disciplinary knowledge.
Selected research courses develop empirical projects and evidence synthesis; none centres the external module’s single-case experimental designs and individual change analysis.
The scheduled UCR courses do not include a required individual pedagogical empirical thesis. Optional independent research is shown separately outside the scheduled credits.
Introductory UCR assessment is placed with Diagnostics. No additional selected module reproduces the advanced child-focused professional assessment and advice sequence.
Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies includes major therapeutic approaches, but its strongest overall placement is Diagnostics. It is not counted a second time here.
Open space remains unspecified; no elective or minor is invented as a comparator course.

comparator.note: The normal programme requires a 6 EC internship, including approved practice or research experience, preparation, reflection and supervision. The course entry also offers a 9 EC variant; this example uses the prescribed 6 EC component. Students arrange an approved host and complete the required information and application training before starting.

comparator.text: Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 1
Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 2
comparator.note: Academic Skills A and B are compulsory in year 1. They carry no separate EC: their workload is credited within the content courses.

Year 2 requires at least 42 first-year EC. Academic Skills C and D are compulsory with no separate EC. Testing and Measurement follows participation in Descriptive Statistics; Inferential Statistics requires passing Descriptive Statistics; Research in Practice requires passing both Descriptive Statistics and Testing and Measurement. Professional Skills 2 requires passing Professional Skills 1.

comparator.text: Empirical Bachelor Thesis in Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.note: The 15 EC empirical thesis follows completion of the first two years, except that one year-2 content course and Academic Skills D may remain. At least nine colloquium points are also required for graduation: five from POW master-thesis presentations, one from a doctorate or inaugural lecture, and three from POW or Comenius lectures or conferences.

Professional Skills 3 requires passing Professional Skills 2 and following Diagnostics. Following means a recorded assessment result. It develops practical child and adolescent assessment and advice skills.

The 30 EC open space remains unspecified. Choices must not overlap the compulsory curriculum. Second- and third-year faculty courses can be selected without extra approval. First-year courses normally need to form part of a completed minor; other choices, skills and language courses require prior Examination Board approval. Exchange also requires approval.

notes.text: UvA offers a dedicated Pedagogical Sciences degree with family and school study, child-focused assessment and professional skills, a required internship and an empirical thesis. UCR can combine developmental psychology, introductory assessment and psychotherapy, social context, research, policy and community teaching. Its options do not reproduce the full pedagogical practice sequence or confer a clinical professional qualification.

audience.programmeDescription: Pedagogical Sciences studies how children and adolescents develop within family, peer, school and wider social environments. The UvA degree combines developmental and pedagogical knowledge with research, professional skills, assessment, an internship and an empirical thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can combine developmental, social and health psychology with research, ethics, policy and community teaching. The dedicated UvA degree provides a more sustained family- and child-focused curriculum and professional practice sequence. The options show different academic priorities; they do not establish professional registration or entry to a particular postgraduate programme.
